label: my-PV AC•THOR – Opportunity Loads
info:
My-PV AC-Thor using s2-resource's built-in D-Bus transport.

**Configuration:** open the `Controller & scheduler` function node and edit `DEVICE_IP` and `LANGUAGE_CODE` at the top of the function.

**My-PV device setup (required):** in the My-PV web interface, go to Device Setup > Control settings and set the control type to **HTTP**. This flow drives the device through `/control.html?power=` and reads `/data.jsn` and `/setup.jsn`.

**Assumed device:** My-PV AC-Thor 9s with three 3000 W heating elements (one per phase, 9 kW total), matching the s2-resource System Description and 3-phase D-Bus measurement.

**Scheduling:** all HTTP traffic is serialized by one scheduler. Normal targets are data.jsn every 2 s, SET power every 4 s, setup.jsn every 45 s, with configurable backoff and three retries.

**Startup safety:** OMBC remains unavailable until the actual device `devmode` has been learned. The flow never defaults an unknown device to either mode. The binary Mode virtual switch itself has `switch_1_initial=0`, but startup switch output is ignored. The controller first learns `devmode` from my-PV, publishes that state to the switch, and only then accepts subsequent switch output as a user command. Normal telemetry requests never contain a `devmode` query parameter.

**Status safety:** Status starts at 7 (`Unknown`) and is set back to 7 after any failed HTTP request or invalid response. A successful `data.jsn` response restores the actual device state.

**Status label language:** supported `LANGUAGE_CODE` values are `en`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, and `nl`.

**Temperature service connectivity:** the Venus OS temperature service starts disconnected. Temperature values are preloaded first; repeated passthrough probes confirm that the virtual node has completed its `start_disconnected` D-Bus initialization before any `msg.connected` command is sent, avoiding a startup presence race. It is marked connected only after a real `temp1` value has been received and while the shared 30-second communication timeout (`commFault`) has not expired. Transient request failures therefore do not disconnect it immediately; it disconnects when the same communication timeout used by S2/control expires.

**Dashboard language:** indicator names, primary labels, the status labels, and the Mode switch name follow `LANGUAGE_CODE` (`en`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `nl`).

**Dashboard updates:** switch, indicators, and temperature-service messages are emitted only when their effective value/settings change.
